action.action-desc: Mr. Schneider (for himself and Mr. Wenstrup) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Ways and Means

form.official-title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend the exemption for telehealth services from certain high deductible health plan rules, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Primary and Virtual Care Affordability Act.

subsection.text: Subparagraph (E) of section 223(c)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking December 31, 2021 and inserting December 31, 2023.
Clause (ii) of section 223(c)(1)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking December 31, 2021 and inserting December 31, 2023.
The amendments made by this section shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: High deductible health plan safe harbor for no deductible for certain primary care services provided during the COVID emergency

subsection.text: Paragraph (2) of section 223(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.header: Safe harbor for absence of deductible for certain primary care services provided during the COVID emergency

clause.text: A plan shall not fail to be treated as a high deductible health plan by reason of failing to have a deductible for primary care services provided by a qualified provider in any plan year beginning on or before December 31, 2023.
For purposes of clause (i), the term primary care services means services provided by primary care practitioners (as defined in section 1833(x)(2)(A)) of the Social Security Act.

For purposes of clause (i), the term qualified provider means a general practitioner, family physician, general internist, obstetrician, gynecologist, pediatrician, geriatric physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant acting in accordance with State laws.

subsection.text: The amendment made by this section shall apply to plan years beginning after December 31, 2019.

The Comptroller General of the United States shall complete a study on the effects of the safe harbor for certain primary care services provided during the COVID emergency under section 223(c)(2)(G) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (as added by section 3).

paragraph.text: Not later than 365 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall provide a report to Congress containing an analysis of the results of the study under subsection (a). Such report shall contain—

subparagraph.text: an analysis of the effects of the safe harbor on—

clause.text: whether plan sponsors opted to incorporate changes to their benefit design;
enrollment in high deductible health plans;
utilization of primary care visits, telehealth visits, emergency department visits, and hospital admissions; and
the rate of employer im­ple­men­ta­tion of flexibilities in changes to benefit design; and

subparagraph.text: comparisons of patient engagement with services for those whose employer incorporated flexibilities into their benefit design and those who did not do so.

paragraph.text: Not later than 365 days after the interim report under paragraph (1) is issued, the Comptroller General of the United States shall provide a final report to Congress containing a comprehensive analysis of the results of the study under subsection (a). Such report shall include updated findings, analyses, and comparisons described in paragraph (1).
